subject: Multi-customer controls discovery — quota, routing & tiering (EdgeFin)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Ruiz <daniel@edgefin.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-02T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Recap: multi-customer controls discovery — EdgeFin / Redwood

Hi Daniel — great conversation this morning, thanks for the time. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next steps.

Call summary (30m):
- Business pain: a small set of customers are consuming disproportionate model tokens and driving costs + noisy behavior that degrades latency for higher-tier customers.
- Current stack: EdgeFin runs a mix of open LLMs on-prem behind an API gateway; tenant identification is via API key; billing is batch-processed and not linked to per-request routing. No per-tenant throttles or tiered routing today.
- Desired outcomes / success criteria (from your side):
  * enforce per-customer monthly token caps + short-term burst limits
  * routing by customer tier to higher/lower-cost model variants to preserve SLOs
  * telemetry for per-tenant latency & cost broken into billable buckets
  * ability to change a tenant's tier dynamically (overrides) and roll back quickly

Key constraints you mentioned:
- Cannot have any PII leave EdgeFin’s VPC for regulated accounts (some tenants require VPC deployment).
- Hard SLO: p95 generation < 350ms for premium tier under typical load.
- Migration timeline: aim for an initial pilot within 6–8 weeks, production rollout in Q4 if pilot is successful.

What Redwood can do (high level):
- Per-tenant quota enforcement at the runtime edge (token accounting per API key), with burst windows and soft/hard thresholds.
- Policy-driven routing: a tenant map drives routing to model variants (quantized/cost-optimized vs high-accuracy variants), plus automatic fallback rules.
- Dynamic tiering via API + console, with audit logs and policy versioning for rollouts.
- Private deployment option for regulated tenants (VPC) and dedicated pools for predictable latency.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) You share a 48–72h sample of tenant traffic (IDs + rough daily token consumption) — helps sizing and quota defaults.
2) We schedule a 60m technical deep dive with Stephanie (runtime) and one of our infra engineers to walk through enforcement and config examples.
3) Redwood to share a brief (1–2 pages) on per-tenant quota semantics and a sample policy template before the deep dive.

Please confirm the priority order above and whether the timeline (pilot in 6–8 weeks) still holds. Also attaching a short brief I referenced.

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134
[Attachment: redwood-multitenancy-brief.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]

From: Daniel Ruiz <daniel@edgefin.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-02T11:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Recap: multi-customer controls discovery — EdgeFin / Redwood

Sean — thanks for the crisp summary. This captures it well. A couple clarifying points and asks from my side:

1) Quota enforcement behavior: can Redwood provide soft limits that surface warnings (and telemetry) before hard throttling kicks in? We want to communicate to customers prior to cutting them off.
2) Dynamic tiering: we need the ability to temporarily elevate a tenant (e.g., during a critical batch job) and then auto-revert after X hours. Is that supported via API or only via console?
3) For the pilot, I will share a CSV with 72h of sample usage (tenant_id, hourly_tokens, peak qps) — attaching now.

Also, procurement asked for a rough pricing band for dedicated pools + per-tenant metering — if you can include a preliminary cost model that maps to our sample usage, that will speed approval.

Availability for the technical deep dive: Tue 9/8 or Thu 9/10 afternoons PT. Preferred attendees: our platform lead (I’ll confirm once I check calendars).

Thanks,
Daniel Ruiz
Head of Platform Engineering, EdgeFin
daniel@edgefin.com
[Attachment: edgefin-tenant-usage-sample.csv]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Ruiz <daniel@edgefin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-02T12:15:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Recap: multi-customer controls discovery — EdgeFin / Redwood

Perfect, Daniel — appreciate the sample file. Quick answers inline and an updated list of concrete next steps below.

1) Soft vs hard limits — yes. We support a staged enforcement model: soft alerts (telemetry + warning headers) -> adaptive throttling window -> hard reject on sustained overages. Soft alerts are configurable per-tenant and can emit to your monitoring or via webhooks.

2) Dynamic tiering / temporary overrides — supported via both API and Console. You can issue a time-bounded override (start/end timestamps) via our Admin API; overrides are audited and can be scheduled/backfilled. We’ll show examples in the tech deep dive.

3) Pricing band for pilot: based on the sample you sent, preliminary estimate is $X–Y/month for a small dedicated pool + per-tenant metering. I’ll work with Neha to produce a 1-page cost sketch tied to your CSV before we lock dates.

Proposed concrete next steps:
- You: confirm who will join the tech deep dive (platform lead + 1 infra) and pick Tue 9/8 2pm PT or Thu 9/10 3pm PT.
- We (Redwood): compile a pilot MMP (mutual action plan) and a 1-page cost estimate; Stephanie will prepare a runtime demo showing quota enforcement and a sample policy template.
- Shared deliverables: pilot MMP (Doc), sample policy JSON, cost sketch, recording of the tech deep dive.

I’ve attached the brief we discussed and a sample policy snippet to this message. If the pilot timeline is still 6–8 weeks we’ll aim to have the MMP within 3 business days.

Suggested meeting: Tue 2026-09-08 14:00 PT — tentative on my calendar. If that works, send the invites and we’ll lock it.

Best,
Sean
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-multitenancy-brief.pdf (PDF)]
[Related link: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/edgefin/recording-20260902.mp4]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-03T09:00:00-04:00
Subject: Fwd: Recap: multi-customer controls discovery — EdgeFin / Redwood

Stef — forwarding the brief and Daniel’s sample usage. Can you please prep the following for Tue 9/8 deep dive: 

- Quick runtime demo (15m) showing per-tenant soft/hard quota enforcement + where warnings surface in telemetry.
- One example policy that routes "premium" tenants to a higher-accuracy model and "standard" tenants to a quantized variant; include rollback steps.
- A suggested default quota profile (monthly tokens + burst limit) based on the attached CSV; I’m putting Neha on the cost sketch.
- Bring one infra person who can speak to private/VPC options and KMS integration.

I’ll confirm the invite if Daniel locks Tue 14:00 PT. Attaching a short prep checklist.

Thanks — Sean
[Attachment: edgefin-prep-checklist.md]
